_comment: Body app, Coach tab (wave 1, Oct 29, 2026). The voice-note capture how-to and what the coach will do. The iPhone steps follow Apple's own Shortcuts and Back Tap help pages; the Android lines are general and were not checked against Google's pages. None of the steps were run on a phone. No model is called in wave 1.

capture.intro: Stephen records a voice note whenever he has an idea: one tap, talk, and the words land as text. Here is one way to set that up.

iphone.name: iPhone, with the Shortcuts app
steps: Open Shortcuts (it comes with the iPhone) and tap + to make a new shortcut.
Add the action Dictate Text. It listens and turns what you say into words.
Add the action Append to Note, pick a note such as Ideas, and give it the Dictated Text.
Name it Voice note, then tap the share button and choose Add to Home Screen.
For one press from anywhere, set it on the Action button (Settings, Action Button, Shortcut) on phones that have one, or on Back Tap (Settings, Accessibility, Touch, Back Tap).

sources.title: Apple, Shortcuts User Guide
sources.says: How to make a shortcut and add it to the Home Screen.

sources.title: Apple, Run shortcuts by tapping the back of iPhone
sources.says: Settings, Accessibility, Touch, Back Tap, then pick Double Tap or Triple Tap and the shortcut.

sources.title: Apple, Use Back Tap on your iPhone
sources.says: Back Tap needs iOS 14 or later.

android.name: Android
steps: Google Keep: tap the microphone, talk, and Keep saves the recording with its words written out.
On a Pixel, the Recorder app writes out what you say as you say it.

capture.tip: One place for every note. Once a week, read them over and move the good ones into your plan.

will: Log what you tell it, the way you'd say it: "chest press, 90 for 12, two left" goes into your Train log.
A morning check-in: today's habits, your water and protein so far, and the one thing to do first.
Nudges you choose, like a breathing break at 1 pm or a glass of water at 3.
Answers about your own numbers: how your water's gone this month, your best streak, last time on the leg press.
chat.privacy: It will only read what you tell it and what the app already keeps for you, and you can turn it off.
